title: Consumer Node Preview 1.0.0-rc1: preview for Fully Decoupled Drupal sites
description: Consumer Node Preview points Drupal's Preview button at your Fully Decoupled frontend, so editors see unsaved changes the way readers will. Druxt Node Preview 0.1.0 is the Nuxt side.

content.html: Press Preview on a Fully Decoupled Drupal site, and Consumer Node Preview 1.0.0-rc1 shows the unsaved page in the frontend your readers will see: the title you just changed and the paragraph you just rewrote, rendered by the site that will publish them, before you save.

In Drupal, a consumer is an app that reads the API. Each one lists the frontends that render its content, and Preview frames one of them. Druxt Node Preview 0.1.0 does the Nuxt side, but any frontend that reads JSON:API can be on the other end.

content.alt: Drupal's preview screen with Frontend, Drupal and JSON:API tabs. The Frontend tab frames the druxtjs.org page Getting started with Druxt inside the site's own header and breadcrumb. A Show changes against the live page toggle is on and reports 2 changes: the title gains the words from zero, and in the first paragraph piece of content is struck through and replaced with page.
content.caption: Two unsaved edits, rendered by the Druxt site readers see. The changes toggle is an early look at the diff work coming next on druxtjs.org.

content.title: Install the Drupal side
content.code:
composer require drupal/jsonapi_node_preview:^1.0@beta drupal/consumer_node_preview:^1.0@RC
drush en consumer_node_preview
content.highlighted: composer require drupal/jsonapi_node_preview:^1.0@beta drupal/consumer_node_preview:^1.0@RC drush en consumer_node_preview

content.html: It builds on JSON:API Node Preview, which serves the unsaved node as a JSON:API document. That module is still in beta, so this release is a candidate. For unsaved paragraphs, also apply the patch from #3367724 with cweagans/composer-patches, as the example site's composer.json does.
Then add a target: a label and a URL template, on the consumer's form under Configuration > Web services > Consumers, or in settings.php when the URL changes per environment:

content.title: settings.php
content.highlighted: $settings['consumer_node_preview'] = [ 'targets' => [ 'frontend' => [ 'label' => 'Frontend', 'url' => 'https://www.example.com/druxt/node/preview?vm=[view_mode]&layout=[layout]#[jsonapi_node_preview]', 'layouts' => ['default', 'preview'], ], ], ];

content.html: Press Preview and the module fills in the view mode and layout from the preview screen's selects, and the address of the unsaved node's JSON:API document, then frames the result on the Frontend tab. Beside it, Drupal is core's own preview, for anything Drupal renders itself, and JSON:API is the raw document: the tab I open first when a field doesn't turn up.

Look at where [jsonapi_node_preview] sits in that template: after the #. Browsers never send the fragment to a server, so the address of an unsaved draft stays out of the frontend's access logs, any CDN in front of it, and the Referer of anything the page loads. Scripts on the page can still read it, so keep error tracking and session replay off the preview route.

Druxt Node Preview only fetches from its own origin, its Drupal site, or origins you list, so a crafted link can't point it at somebody else's server. It also tells shared caches and search engines to keep nothing of the preview route.

paragraphs.title: Keeping the draft out of the logs

content.html: Next.js for Drupal previews a saved revision through a signed draft-mode request, and that link can go to a reviewer. Consumer Node Preview previews what's still in the edit form, before a revision exists, so the preview belongs to the editor who pressed the button.

paragraphs.title: Why not preview a saved draft?

content.html: On the same site, the preview page fetches with the editor's own session. Core's session cookie is SameSite=Lax, so that works when both share a parent domain, like www.example.com and cms.example.com, and Drupal's CORS config names the frontend and allows credentials:

content.title: services.yml, same site
content.code:
parameters:
  cors.config:
    enabled: true
    allowedHeaders: ['*']
    allowedMethods: ['GET']
    allowedOrigins: ['https://www.example.com']
    supportsCredentials: true
content.highlighted: parameters: cors.config: enabled: true allowedHeaders: ['*'] allowedMethods: ['GET'] allowedOrigins: ['https://www.example.com'] supportsCredentials: true

content.html: For a frontend on another domain, such as example.vercel.app, the preview reads with a token instead. Install Simple OAuth, then on the consumer's form turn on the Authorization Code grant, and give its Authorization Code settings a scope for your editors' role. With only a client credentials scope, the preview gets a 403.

End the target with ;token=[preview_token], and in settings.php name its consumer with 'consumer' => 'my-frontend'. Each Preview then adds a token to the fragment. It has the editor's access and lasts 15 minutes, and Druxt Node Preview strips it from the page's address as soon as the page loads. The page sends it without a cookie, so the CORS config changes two lines:

content.title: services.yml, token route
content.code:
parameters:
  cors.config:
    # As the same-site config, with these two lines changed:
    allowedOrigins: ['*']
    supportsCredentials: false
content.highlighted: parameters: cors.config: # As the same-site config, with these two lines changed: allowedOrigins: ['*'] supportsCredentials: false

content.html: On either route, the preview page has to let Drupal frame it: no X-Frame-Options there, and Drupal's origin in any frame-ancestors rule.
On a Druxt site, the page at the other end is a Nuxt module, and it can register its own target:

content.title: nuxt.config.js
content.highlighted: // npm install druxt-site @druxt-contrib/node-preview export default { modules: ['@druxt-contrib/node-preview', 'druxt-site'], druxt: { baseUrl: 'https://cms.example.com', proxy: { api: true }, nodePreview: { layouts: ['default', 'preview'], register: { url: 'https://example.vercel.app', consumer: 'my-frontend', // The consumer's client ID. token: true, }, }, }, }

content.html: With the secret of a consumer set up for Simple OAuth in DRUXT_NODE_PREVIEW_CLIENT_SECRET, the module adds its target to Drupal whenever Nuxt starts up, and removes it when the server stops. A target with token on reads with a token instead, and with Druxt's API proxy on, that request stays on the frontend's origin, so Drupal's CORS doesn't need changing for it.

The preview itself goes in the Druxt Vuex store before DruxtEntity resolves, so it renders through the same components as the live page. Each listed layout needs a file in layouts/ that renders <Nuxt />, and the editor picks one from the Layout select.

Druxt Node Preview is for Nuxt 2, which is end of life, and its build needs Node 16. Like the rest of Druxt's modules, it stays 0.x until Druxt reaches 1.0.0. Nothing in the URL template is Druxt-specific, though. This is the core of a preview page in Nuxt 3, Next or Astro:

content.title: A preview page for any other frontend
content.highlighted: // Runs in the browser: the fragment never reaches a server. // The origins this page may fetch a preview from. const allowed = ['https://cms.example.com'] // Some routers turn https:// into https:/ inside a hash. const hash = decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)) const [address, token] = hash .replace(/^(https?):\/(?!\/)/, '$1://') .split(';token=') const endpoint = new URL(address) if (!allowed.includes(endpoint.origin)) { throw new Error(`Refusing a preview from ${endpoint.origin}`) } const response = await fetch(endpoint, { // A token target reads without the cookie. credentials: token ? 'omit' : 'include', headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.api+json', ...(token && { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }), }, }) if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Preview failed: HTTP ${response.status}`) const { data, included } = await response.json() // Render data and included with the components a live page uses.

paragraphs.title: Druxt renders it like any other page

content.html: Use your site's own HTTP client if it adds headers to requests to Drupal. A bare fetch() skips them, and a preview can show the wrong content with no error.

Watch for components that load their own data. The module sets a flag while a preview is open, so a component like druxtjs.org's docs page, which refetched its paragraphs, can skip that request and keep the unsaved ones.

Unsaved paragraphs come through with the patch on #3367724, which druxtjs.org runs as a Composer patch. If you preview paragraphs, please test it on your site and leave a review. A tested review is what it needs to land.

content.description: Consumer Node Preview's code is on GitHub, and its releases and issue queue are on Drupal.org. If your editors work on a Fully Decoupled site, sponsorship is what moves the diff work up the list.
Druxt Node Preview is on GitHub. Its end-to-end suite builds a Drupal site with both modules and previews through a real Druxt frontend.

content.html: The changes toggle in the screenshot is an early look from druxtjs.org, and diffs are the next sprint.
If your frontend sits on another domain from Drupal, is a 15-minute token long enough for the way your editors preview?
